Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 9
Subject: GRADE
Strand: Science Braille Notation
Topic 7.1: Representation of Atomic Structure in Braille • Ion formation • Chemical formulae • Chemical Equations
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Representation of Atomic Structure in Braille • Ion formation • Chemical formulae • Chemical Equations, part of Science Braille Notation in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 9 GRADE.

Key inquiry question: How are ions represented in Braille?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. manipulate tactile structures of elements showing formation of ions on a braille work card. For example, tactile structures representing lithium, calcium, chloride and aluminum ions,

2. identify braille representations of ions showing arrangement of electrons and charge number on the braille work card,

3. write braille representations of ions showing the charge number using braille writing equipment and materials. Learners share and critique each other’s work,

4. identify chemical formulas of compounds and radicals in braille (such as Fe2O3, Al2(SO4)3, NaCl),

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. manipulate tactile structures of elements showing formation of ions on a braille work card. For example, tactile structures representing lithium, calcium, chloride and aluminum ions,
2. identify braille representations of ions showing arrangement of electrons and charge number on the braille work card,
3. write braille representations of ions showing the charge number using braille writing equipment and materials. Learners share and critique each other’s work,
4. identify chemical formulas of compounds and radicals in braille (such as Fe2O3, Al2(SO4)3, NaCl),

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Representation of Atomic Structure in Braille • Ion formation • Chemical formulae • Chemical Equations together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and Collaboration: the learner interacts effectively with peers while working in groups to prepare tactile

structures showing ion formation using locally available materials.

● Creativity and Innovation: the learner prepares a tactile structure showing ion formation using locally available resources

and braille writing materials.

Values:
● Unity: the learner collaborates harmoniously with one another during group activities.

● Responsibility: as learners take care of digital devices such as refreshable braille displays.
